summary: BLUT and Katana process adapters are merged into OpenWarrant; Katana native receipt interfaces merged upstream at 5a735133 with all hosted checks passing. A candidate core collector enrollment codec checks exact current authority, human-admin signature policy, executable/provider identity and explicit Warrant scope. Eight synthetic-adapter controls and 705 core regressions pass. Protected cryptographic enrollment workflow, operator custody, activation, native collector wiring and independent/participant qualification remain open. A candidate reference OpenSSH transport verifies exact enrollment bytes; four crypto/SDK controls, 17 process regressions and all-target/all-feature CLI Clippy pass, with two native-provider cases explicitly not run in this observation. Protected activation and collector wiring remain open. The candidate execution loader checks actual UID and protected paths, authenticates enrollment, and rechecks authority per use. Three loading controls, four crypto controls, an authority CLI regression, an explicitly run two-UID namespace roundtrip and strict CLI Clippy pass. Core enrollment is merged at d05cf826 after the full CI gate. Activation, native collector wiring, launch fencing and operator/independent qualification remain open. Prospective v2 authority activation now checks current human signer kind and current presence policy; retained history remains unchanged. Nine SDK authority controls, 707 core tests, three authority CLI unit tests and strict all-target/all-feature SDK/CLI Clippy pass. These software fixtures do not establish operator deployment or human review. The focused authentication plant passes 28 checks, including refusal of ordinary-signature presence downgrade. Eight integration regressions and a provisioned two-UID roundtrip pass; the initial default-scratch namespace failure is retained separately. Explicit public authority metadata sharing is implemented as an opt-in normal-mode bootstrap flag; private storage remains the default. Seven collector controls and the actual normal CLI bootstrap/activation two-UID namespace fixture pass. The fixture observes read access, denied authority writes, UID mismatch refusal and signed revocation; it does not establish human review or host deployment qualification. Candidate operator-selected collector activation now retains signed configurations and selection events. Active execution loading and per-use checks bind actual UID, fresh authority and exact selection. The full CLI suite passes 441 unit and 213 integration tests (four deliberately ignored); the explicit normal-mode separate-user activation, refusal, replay, replacement and revocation controls pass. Strict all-target/all-feature CLI Clippy passes. These are performer software/namespace observations, not qualified deployment or human review. Verifier availability classification is corrected: a valid signature with missing account metadata now stays UNKNOWN instead of being falsely called invalid. Seven collector controls, the explicit namespace experiment, one classification control, 17 process/capture regressions and strict CLI Clippy pass; known cryptographic refusals remain distinct.
next_steps: Finish protected enrollment drafting/signing and native collector workflow wiring; selected configuration does not authenticate the acting collector or fence a native launch.
Wire trusted collector policy and native verifier into the actual workflow request/response path; preserve UNKNOWN for absent custody, spend or confinement observations.
Complete actual provider integrations, independent verification and participant qualification without inventing acceptance.
